title: Writing Effective Commit Messages
learning_objectives: Write commit messages following Conventional Commits format
Craft clear, concise commit descriptions under 50 characters
Compose commit bodies that explain what and why, not how
Use imperative mood correctly in commit subjects
Choose appropriate commit types for different kinds of changes
Reference GitHub issues in commit footers
Amend commits to fix message mistakes before pushing
Apply commit message best practices to CatchBook development
outline: Review: Conventional Commits structure from L01
The 50/72 rule: subject line and body formatting
Imperative mood: 'Add feature' not 'Added feature' or 'Adds feature'
Subject line guidelines: capitalize first word, no period, be specific
When to include a commit body: complex changes, non-obvious decisions
Writing effective bodies: explain motivation and context
Commit footer syntax: issue references (Closes #123, Refs #456)
Common mistakes: vague descriptions, mixed concerns, missing type
The art of atomic commits: one logical change per commit
Amending commits: git commit --amend for message fixes
Interactive examples: improve bad commit messages
Hands-on: Write 5 conventional commits for CatchBook README improvements
Hands-on: Amend a commit message to follow conventions
Hands-on: Write commit with body explaining design decision
outline_structure_notes: Sections 1-11 are conceptual/examples. Sections 12-14 are hands-on exercises.
checkpoint_placement_guidance: After section 5 (body writing), after section 9 (atomic commits), after section 11 (examples), after final hands-on exercise (section 14).

catchbook_context.feature: Professional commit messages for all CatchBook changes
catchbook_context.deliverable: Series of well-formatted commits improving CatchBook README documentation

criteria: All commits follow Conventional Commits format
Appropriate commit types selected for each change
At least one commit includes well-written body
Issue references formatted correctly in footers

resources.title: How to Write a Git Commit Message (Chris Beams)
The Seven Rules of a Great Git Commit Message

professor_constraints: Provide 10-15 'bad commit message' examples for learner to improve
Use actual CatchBook feature work for commit examples (species model, photo upload, etc.)
Show git log output before and after adopting conventions
Demonstrate git commit --amend workflow carefully (emphasize 'before pushing' caveat)
Address anxiety about 'overthinking' commit messages with efficiency tips
Show how descriptive commits help future debugging
Encourage learner to write commit messages as if explaining to teammate
